_note: THE WAIT NAMES THE RECENT BAND, not the overlay root. The band only
renders when a recent list EXISTS (`showRecent`), and the probe case had
no stored list, so the screen the board draws — RECENT · 12 over a tile
grid — had never been on screen. `withRecentIcons` seeds it from
`getAllIcons()` rather than from typed-out names, because `readRecent`
resolves each through `getIconByName` and silently drops what it cannot
find: a renamed icon would shrink the band without failing anything.
BOARD WON: 147:2 gives this drill-in the drawer's --flowbite/gray/100
edge and the overlay drew no border at all, so its computed border-color
was #000000, the initial value. Third time this defect has been found on
the same family (144:2 on SlimLauncher, 146:2 on the asset detail).
Also 147:13, the category trigger: 12/18 where it shipped 13; 147:14, the
'N categories' mono count, which had no line-height at all and computed
`normal`; and 220:827's 8 gap on the section header, absent because the
label grows with flex-1 and hides the difference until the count is short.
THE TILE GRID IS NOT JOINED, and it is the one thing this board most looks
like it should settle. 147:18/147:19 draw FIVE tiles up on a 16 inset with
an 11.2 gap and 1.6 side padding — fractions that are the export of a
space-between row, not a designed gutter (5x40 = 200 inside 248 leaves 48,
which is exactly 2x1.6 + 4x11.2). Board 75:25 draws the same grid SIX up
on a 12 gutter with tiles that fill their track, IconBrowserOverlay's own
docstring has said '6-up grid' since it was written, and boards.json has
75:2 recorded drift-fixed against the shipped six-up markup as of
2026-09-08. Two boards disagree; the verified one stands.
NOT JOINED, and why: 147:10, the search field — chrome-ui TextInput, which
boards.json holds at authority=open:input-fill; its w-248 is also the 280
frame less the row's own 16 inset, i.e. the row's arithmetic and not a
decision about the control. 147:9, the row AROUND it, carries a
border + radius on a full-bleed 36-high frame while the 28-high field
inside it carries its own — two nested rounded rectangles is an export
artifact, not a design, and the only real fact in the node (h36) is joined
through the code's own row anyway. 147:11 is the placeholder, which lives
on the same control. 1720:17378 is a hotspot.
FOUND AND FIXED, and it was shipping: the RECENT band measured 16 tall
against its own `tw:h-7`. It is a flex item in a column whose content
overflows and it carried no `shrink-0`, so the browser compressed it — on
every screen that has recents, in the live product, invisibly to the test
suite. `h-7` was right; nothing was enforcing it.
